note: Bulk OSM imports that applied natural=hot_spring to features that are not hot springs. Unlike data/private/exclusions.json (which is secret by design), this list is public: it is a claim about upstream data quality and it should be arguable. Records matched here are quarantined to data/suspect.json, never deleted.

rule_definitions.attribute-free: The element carries no tag other than `natural=hot_spring` and a name (in any language). No temperature, operator, website, wikidata, elevation, source, address, or any other attribute. A genuine spring that anyone has actually visited nearly always picks up at least one of these.

imports.reason: A water-point dataset imported with the wrong tag. The Baghdad cluster (33.0-33.6N, 44.0-44.7E) alone holds 263 nodes named after city districts, checkpoints and villages -- 'قرية الزجالبة' (Zajalba village), 'سيطرة محسن' (Muhsin checkpoint), 'مدخل جديد تبليط' (new paved entrance). Central Baghdad has no geothermal field. Elsewhere the names are bare well registry numbers ('0061', '0126').
imports.keeps: Properly attributed springs in Iraq are unaffected. Hammam al-Alil, a real thermal bath south of Mosul, carries attributes and survives the filter.

imports.reason: Same failure mode. 424 attribute-free nodes spread across the whole country with personal and settlement names ('jaboreen', 'OMAR', 'ابراهيم البولهيس'), which is the signature of a humanitarian water-point survey, not a geothermal one.
Same failure mode. 158 attribute-free nodes named after families and villages ('آل ميقان', 'ال مرضي').

Irrigation boreholes in the Kufra basin (28.5-29.5N, 19.0-20.5E), named with well identifiers ('6J659', '-193c', '291-287-283-281-282'). These sit on the centre-pivot fields of the Great Man-Made River scheme and are groundwater abstraction points.

how_to_dispute: If you know one of these clusters is real, open an issue with a source. The quarantined records are kept in data/suspect.json with full provenance, so reinstating them is a one-line change to this file rather than a re-ingest.
